domain_assessment.role: Maintenance-of-Way Supervisor overseeing a panel tie gang
domain_assessment.objective: Safely replace defective rail, renew ties, restore track geometry, and lift a slow order within a 60-hour possession before a contracted freight surge.
domain_assessment.incident_type: Time-constrained response to an ultrasonic rail-flaw indication involving scope estimation, method selection, status reporting, and a go/no-go reopening decision before formal geometry verification.

decision_points.summary: On Tuesday, the supervisor scopes the work and commits to a 60-hour schedule using the recent fair tie rating and standard production rates without retrieving the accessible five-year defect-growth history.
evidence_before: Ultrasonic flaw-car indication at mile post 47.3
Two-week-old inspection rating ties as fair with some deterioration
One shared tamper and ballast regulator
evidence_after: Wednesday tie count exceeds the planned scope
The work scope must be revised during the possession
goals_constraints: Complete rail replacement and tie renewal safely
Restore service before the holiday freight surge
alternatives: Retrieve and incorporate the five-year defect history
Use a more conservative scope estimate
Proceed using the current inspection and standard production rate
decision_points.decision_basis: The recent rating was treated as sufficiently current and the production table as the default planning basis; retrieving the longer history was viewed as delaying mobilization.
decision_points.time_pressure: High, because the crew was mobilized the same afternoon for a fixed possession.
decision_points.uncertainty: The actual tie condition, recurring flaw history, weather impact, and available production margin were incompletely known.

decision_points.summary: On Wednesday, the group selects an accelerated recovery method after discovering more rotted ties than expected.
evidence_before: Foreman's proposal to add a tamper pass and reduce ballast dwell time
Inspectors' initial questions about dwell time and compaction
Site report identifying worse-than-typical subgrade drainage
evidence_after: The group adopts the faster method
The group becomes more supportive of acceleration than members were at the start of the discussion
goals_constraints: Recover time lost to increased scope
Maintain adequate compaction and geometry quality
alternatives: Maintain normal dwell time and accept schedule slippage
Use an extra tamper pass and reduce dwell time
Reassess drainage and site-specific conditions before changing the method
decision_points.decision_basis: A remembered successful prior curve increased confidence in the accelerated option, while a material drainage difference was not brought back into the discussion.
decision_points.time_pressure: High, because the revised scope had consumed part of the fixed outage window.
decision_points.uncertainty: It remained unclear whether the shortened dwell time was suitable for the current drainage and ballast conditions.

decision_points.summary: On Thursday, the supervisor frames progress and delay causes for the regional engineering manager, who approves retaining the existing timeline.
evidence_before: Some segments on pace while the overall work remains behind the revised plan
evidence_after: The regional engineering manager approves continuation of the existing timeline
goals_constraints: Retain approval for the completion timeline
alternatives: Report both external disruptions and the original scope-estimation miss
Credit internal execution and the accelerated method for favorable progress
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant reported genuine external setbacks, credited internal performance for favorable segments, and did not report the initial scope miss as a contributor to delay.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate, during an active possession with limited remaining slack.
decision_points.uncertainty: The remaining schedule recovery and final completion time were still uncertain.

decision_points.summary: On Friday, six hours before the freight opening, the supervisor lifts the slow order without a completed geometry-car pass.
evidence_before: Geometry car had not completed its pass
Manual gauge spot checks were clean
A financial contractual penalty would follow continued restriction
Hand-inspection rounds and a reduced-speed pilot train were available
The roadmaster stated that those measures would not provide the geometry car's continuous profile
evidence_after: The geometry car later reports the segment within tolerance
alternatives: Hold the slow order until a geometry-car pass
Lift the slow order using manual checks and compensating inspection measures
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant explicitly weighted avoiding the immediate penalty more heavily than waiting for open-ended formal verification and judged the compensating measures sufficient despite their known limits.
decision_points.time_pressure: Very high; six hours remained before the contracted freight window.
decision_points.uncertainty: The available manual checks and pilot run could not establish the continuous geometry information the geometry car would provide.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: There is a longer defect history on that segment in our system, going back five years, that tracks flaw growth over time. I didn't pull it. At the time it felt like it'd just slow down getting the crew mobilized.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Tuesday scoping follow-up concerning the five-year defect history.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant declines to retrieve accessible and decision-relevant information that could reveal a less favorable scope, instead proceeding from the more reassuring recent inspection rating.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Rapid mobilization may justify relying initially on recent inspection data. However, the omitted information directly concerns recurring flaw growth at the same location and would likely have changed scope, making ordinary triage an incomplete explanation.

revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the accessible-history, perceived-delay, and recent-rating contrast.
preserve: The two-week-old fair rating
The accessible five-year history
The fixed possession and mobilization constraint
avoid_creating: An explicit statement that the participant already knew the history would show severe deterioration

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: I used our standard production rate for a 500-foot renewal — so many ties an hour with a full crew — and built a 60-hour schedule off that, plus the fair rating.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Tuesday initial scope and schedule account.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant commits to a typical production schedule without adjusting for known local deterioration, forecast rain, shared equipment, and uncertainty in actual tie condition.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A standard production-rate table is a legitimate planning baseline. The bias is supported by the unadjusted commitment despite multiple known schedule-relevant uncertainties, not by use of a standard table itself.

revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the standard-rate schedule commitment and the stated absence of meaningful contingency adjustment.
preserve: The standard production-rate table as a legitimate baseline
The distinct evidence-avoidance mechanism for rt7_01
The later discovery of higher-than-planned tie counts
avoid_creating: A claim that standard production rates are inherently biased

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: By the end, everybody was more on board with running fast than any one of us had been at the start of that meeting.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: After group discussion, collective confidence in the accelerated and risk-bearing option becomes stronger than the participants' initial positions.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Groups can rationally converge after sharing useful evidence. Here, the confidence shift follows a weakly comparable anecdote while a material drainage difference is not reconsidered, supporting polarization rather than ordinary consensus alone.

revision.location: Decision point 2, group discussion after the prior-curve anecdote.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the explicit contrast between the group's initial uncertainty and its stronger final support for acceleration.
preserve: The foreman's proposal
The inspectors' initial questions
The separate individual analogy mechanism for rt7_04
avoid_creating: An implication that any team agreement is bias
A second group-polarization event at the status call

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: One of the inspectors mentioned a similar-looking curve we'd worked three years back... it held up fine long-term... Our site report from the day before had actually flagged the subgrade drainage at 47.3 as worse than typical for that district.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Wednesday method-selection account and follow-up on prior-curve comparability.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: A remembered prior job is used as a risk-relevant analogue despite a documented drainage difference that limits the reliability of that comparison.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Experienced analogical reasoning can be appropriate in maintenance work. The bias is supported because a material causal difference in drainage was not integrated into the similarity judgment.

revision.location: Decision point 2, prior-curve anecdote and drainage comparison.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the contrast between the remembered successful curve and the unaddressed drainage warning.
preserve: The practical relevance of prior operational experience
The distinction from group-level polarization
avoid_creating: A suggestion that all experience-based judgment is invalid

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: I told him we'd had a late ballast delivery and lost some hours to a rain delay overnight... For the segments that were tracking on pace, I credited the crew's execution and the call to add the extra tamper pass... I didn't bring [the original scope estimate] up in that call.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Thursday status-call account and follow-up on the omitted scope estimate.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: Within one mixed-outcome account, schedule slippage is attributed to external events while favorable performance is attributed to internal execution and the team's method choice; the participant omits the initial internal scope-estimation contribution.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The rain and late ballast delivery were genuine external disruptions, and execution may genuinely have supported on-pace segments. The bias rests on the asymmetric attribution and omission of the initial planning shortfall.

revision.location: Decision point 3, Thursday regional-manager status call.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the mixed attribution pattern and the later acknowledgement that the original scope estimate contributed to the delay.
preserve: The factual occurrence of rain and late ballast delivery
The possibility that crew execution and the extra tamper pass had some value
The regional manager's approval
avoid_creating: A claim that external causes were fabricated

target_occurrence_audit.bias: Loss Aversion or Loss Framing effect
target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: I knew the geometry car would give us a continuous read across the whole segment that manual checks just can't match, but with that loss already sitting right in front of us and the verification still open-ended, avoiding the hit was what drove the call more than anything else.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Friday go/no-go explanation, immediately after the participant identifies the contractual penalty.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant explicitly assigns greater decision weight to avoiding the immediate and concrete contractual loss than to preserving the safety margin provided by pending, more complete verification.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The contractual penalty is a legitimate operational consideration, and the participant had some compensating risk information. However, the participant directly acknowledges that the geometry car provides distinct verification and states that avoiding the loss drove the decision more than any other consideration.

revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the comparative weighting statement that distinguishes the immediate penalty from the still-open formal verification.
preserve: The real contractual penalty
The formal-verification alternative
The distinct mitigation-confidence mechanism for rt7_07
avoid_creating: A claim that safety was knowingly disregarded
A second loss-framing episode at an earlier decision point

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: The roadmaster pointed out that the hand rounds and the pilot train wouldn't give us the same continuous profile the car would, but I figured between what we already had and those extra rounds, we'd catch anything that mattered.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Friday go/no-go explanation, following the roadmaster's statement about limitations of the compensating measures.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant discounts an identified coverage limitation and overestimates the ability of manual checks, hand inspections, and a reduced-speed pilot train to detect all material geometry problems without the geometry-car pass.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The measures are legitimate risk controls and may detect some hazards. The bias is supported because the participant receives a specific warning that they cannot provide equivalent continuous profiling but nevertheless assumes they would catch every issue that mattered.

revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain both the roadmaster's specific limitation and the participant's confidence that the extra checks would catch any material issue.
preserve: The legitimate partial value of manual checks and reduced-speed pilot operations
The geometry car's distinct continuous-profile capability
The separate loss-framing mechanism for rt7_06
avoid_creating: A claim that the mitigating controls were useless
A new authority-pressure or obedience-bias mechanism
Outcome-based justification from the next-day geometry result

bias_level_counts.bias: Loss Aversion or Loss Framing effect

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: Nobody brought that back up once the other curve got mentioned. It just didn't come up again.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The discussion appears to favor the anecdote supporting acceleration while a drainage fact that weakens the analogy receives no further attention.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The drainage point may have been omitted because of limited meeting time or because participants believed it had already been considered. The evidence is also substantially embedded in the intended Experience Bias and Group Polarization occurrences.

nonbias_cues.cue: The actual tie count was higher than planned.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A poor outcome or inaccurate estimate is not itself evidence of bias. It is relevant only because the prior evidence-selection and schedule-estimation mechanisms are described.

nonbias_cues.cue: Rain, late ballast delivery, and shared equipment.
nonbias_cues.location: Initial constraints and Thursday status call.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: These are genuine operational constraints and external disruptions that may rationally affect schedule performance.
Standard production rates are appropriate base-rate information. The supported Planning Fallacy concerns failure to adjust for known local uncertainty, not use of the rate table.

nonbias_cues.cue: The geometry car later found the track within tolerance.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A favorable later outcome does not demonstrate that lifting the slow order before formal verification was justified, nor does it demonstrate that the earlier decision was biased.

nonbias_cues.location: Follow-up answers about defect history and status reporting.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Retrospective reflection is not automatically hindsight bias. The participant does not claim that the later information was obvious or fully predictable at the time.

nonbias_cues.cue: Manual gauge checks, hand rounds, and a reduced-speed pilot train.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: These are plausible partial safeguards. They support Illusion of Control only because the participant explicitly discounts their known inability to provide the geometry car's continuous profile.

causal_claims.claim: Retrieving the five-year defect history would likely have led to a heavier initial scope and schedule.
causal_claims.support: The participant states that recurring flaw growth would probably have changed the initial plan.
causal_claims.assessment: Plausible self-reported counterfactual, but not independently verified.

causal_claims.claim: The contractual penalty materially caused the decision to lift the slow order before the geometry-car pass.
causal_claims.support: The participant states that avoiding the penalty drove the call more than anything else and says waiting would have been more likely without the penalty.
causal_claims.assessment: Strongly supported as a principal contributor to the decision.

causal_claims.claim: The prior-curve anecdote influenced the group toward an accelerated method.
causal_claims.support: The participant reports that the room's mood shifted after the anecdote and that the group became more supportive of acceleration.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported, though based on a single participant's account of the group process.

causal_claims.claim: The extra tamper pass and crew execution caused on-pace performance in certain segments.
causal_claims.support: The participant credited those factors in the Thursday status call.
causal_claims.assessment: Not causally isolated; segment-specific conditions, weather, material timing, and scope variation remain plausible contributors.

correlation_causation_risks: The next-day within-tolerance geometry-car result must not be treated as proof that lifting the slow order early was the correct decision.
On-pace segments do not independently establish that the extra tamper pass or crew execution caused schedule recovery.
The prior curve's successful outcome does not establish its comparability to mile post 47.3, particularly given the drainage difference.
causal_audit.changed_variable: The interview includes informal counterfactual probes involving availability of the five-year defect history, existence of the contractual penalty, and presence of the prior-curve anecdote.
causal_audit.explanation: The counterfactual probes are coherent elicitation devices rather than a controlled paired-scenario design. The participant appropriately distinguishes the eventual acceptable geometry outcome from the quality of the earlier authorization decision.

global_revision_constraints: Keep the Friday mechanisms distinct: rt7_06 concerns loss-weighting in the choice, while rt7_07 concerns overestimation of compensating-control coverage.
Do not use the favorable geometry-car result as retrospective evidence that the Friday authorization was correct.
Do not convert the operational safety tension into an implausible explicit willingness to disregard safety.
